title: Situational AI & Situation Awareness
question: How does Situational AI relate to existing models of situation awareness, including Endsley’s framework, and where does it depart from them?
lede: Evolution of the idea, related models and Endsley’s Situation Awareness framework.
intro: One of five explorations from the summer of 2026, when UT Dallas students worked with Mindspace AI on questions emerging from Situational AI. This one traces the evolution of the idea, the models related to it, and how it relates to Endsley’s Situation Awareness framework.
sections: What this exploration expected to find about the relationship between Situational AI and prior models of situation awareness.
The models examined, and how the comparison with Endsley’s framework was structured.
What the comparison found, and where Situational AI departs from prior models.
What the comparison could not resolve, and what it suggests next.

title: Can Situations Make AI More Efficient?
question: Can situation recognition reduce context and prompt needs and enable smaller, efficient models?
lede: Situation recognition, context reduction and smaller models.
intro: One of five explorations from the summer of 2026, when UT Dallas students worked with Mindspace AI on questions emerging from Situational AI. This one investigates whether explicit situation recognition can reduce the context a model needs, and whether that lets smaller models do the work.
sections: What this exploration expected: how much context an explicit situation layer could remove, and at what cost.
Why context size matters, and what prior work says about reduction.
Experimental setup: tasks, models compared, how context was reduced, and what was measured.
What the experiments showed, and where efficiency gains held or failed.

title: RiskPulse + Situational AI
question: Can situation recognition be applied to emerging organizational risk?
lede: Applying situation recognition to emerging organizational risk.
intro: One of five explorations from the summer of 2026, when UT Dallas students worked with Mindspace AI on questions emerging from Situational AI. This one is a working application: RiskPulse, which applies situation recognition to emerging organizational risk.
sections: What RiskPulse expected situation recognition to add over signal monitoring alone.
The problem: risks that only mean something together, and only for a particular observer.
Architecture, the situations it recognizes, the signals it uses, and how a recognized situation shapes the response.
What the demonstration shows and what was observed.

title: Exploratory Situational AI Application
question: What does an application built on situation-centric concepts look like in practice?
intro: One of five explorations from the summer of 2026, when UT Dallas students worked with Mindspace AI on questions emerging from Situational AI. This one is an exploratory application of Situational AI, presented with a live demo.
sections: What the application expected situation-centric concepts to change.
Architecture, the situations it recognizes, the signals it uses, and how a recognized situation shapes the response.
What the demonstration shows and what was observed.

title: The Student Exploration
question: What did the student exploration of Situational AI reveal: the journey, the questions and the lessons?
lede: The journey, questions and lessons emerging from the summer work.
intro: One of five explorations from the summer of 2026, when UT Dallas students worked with Mindspace AI on questions emerging from Situational AI. This one steps back from any single project to describe the journey itself: the questions the students brought, the ones the work raised, and the lessons that emerged.
sections: How the summer unfolded: what the students started with and how the work took shape.
The questions that emerged across the five explorations, including the ones the summer did not answer.
What the students learned about Situational AI, about research, and about building with an idea that is still being defined.
